current.text: He has a hamstring injury that may cost him the start of the season. He missed media day for a health issue and was set to miss the preseason. When he will be available is unknown.
He re-signed with Golden State for 3 years and about 40 million USD with a player option, with 20 million USD guaranteed.
The plan is for him to start at center when healthy. The latest team projection, made while he is out, has Al Horford starting at center.
He made the top 100 last season in 24 minutes a game and should play more this season.
He is called the second best player on the Warriors while Jimmy Butler is out. Butler is out for at least half the season.

Do not draft him in the top 100. He could be a top 70 player over about 40 games, which makes him worth a look around pick 150. One expert calls him his biggest Warriors fade because of the health uncertainty.
Drop him if he keeps missing games.
The Warriors have 15 back-to-backs this season, tied for second most. Their schedule is good for playoffs that end March 28.
Because he is not expected to play back-to-backs, one note projects him for about 8 games instead of 11 in its playoff window. That is no reason to avoid him at his price.
The Warriors may treat this season as a gap year. They are worried about lottery odds and may rest veterans.
Experts call the Warriors a bad team and expect their players to fade as the season goes on.
The Warriors have very poor depth and struggle to field a 10-man rotation, so minutes should go up across the rotation.

durable.text: He has a long record of missed games. An ongoing mystery illness caused availability problems last season, and he also has knee and ankle issues.
He is not expected to play back-to-backs.
He is very good per game when he plays and gets overlooked in fantasy because of his availability. Experts put his per-game value around the top 40 to 60.
He is a stretch center. He makes many threes for a center, shoots a strong FT% for his position and adds good blocks.

note: The market has dropped him to almost nothing. He ranks 154 on Yahoo with a 1.0 USD average cost and 80 on ESPN, while our league paid 21 USD for him last season. As a 1 to 3 USD flyer he adds threes from the center spot, blocks and a good FT% for a big, and no category is weak enough to rule out any build. Early in the season, check the hamstring and his Yahoo status (he can only use an IL slot once listed Out or worse), whether he takes back the starting job from Horford, and his minutes. Drop him if the absences keep piling up.
